author: Parshall, Jonathan; Tully, Anthony; and contributors
title: Imperial Japanese Navy Page (combinedfleet.com)
notes:
The website of the authors of source:parshall-tully-2005, and the working notes behind it: ship-by-ship service records of the Imperial Japanese Navy, translations, and the long-running arguments about Midway and Pearl Harbor. Self-published, and cited here for exactly one thing — Parshall's own restatement of his Naval War College Review argument about Fuchida, in the rebuttal page answering Martin Bennett, which is the only place his wording could actually be read from this environment. Cited as a historian's own statement of his position, never as evidence for what happened. The page carries no publication date.

Also read from the site, 30 August 2026: the Hiryū tabular record of movement (combinedfleet.com/hiryu.htm), quoted for the seventy men marooned aboard at Midway, "only thirty-five are eventually rescued by the U.S. Navy, including her Chief Engineer" — cited by the epilogue's closing beat beside the Naval Historical Center's account of the rescue.
